Definition: foolishness, i.e. (morally) wickedness; concretely, a crime; by extension, punishment
BiblicalUsage: Shechem's sons call the defiling of Dinah folly in Israel, and the law calls for the stoning of the woman who commits folly in her father's house. Tamar begs Amnon not to do this folly, and Isaiah says the vile person will speak folly and work iniquity.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe folly in the Bible is never a small mistake: it is the crime that tears a family and a nation, and God calls it what it is so that I will not call it anything smaller. I must not call folly a mistake when God calls it a crime, and I must not treat lightly what tore a family apart.
